meta.title: Window Tint Questions and Answers | BC Glass & Tint
meta.description: Answers to common window tint, home film, windshield chip repair, clear bra, ceramic coating and blinds questions for BC Glass & Tint in Boulder City, NV.

v3.lede: Everything customers ask about tint, film, glass and our work.

search.label: Search the questions
search.empty: No question matches that. Call or text us and we will give you a straight answer.

items.question: How much does window tint cost?
items.answer: It depends on real variables: how many windows, the size and shape of the glass, and whether old film has to come off first. Removing failed film is its own step and is a big reason prices vary. See the price guide, or call or text us your year, make and model, or a home window count, for a free quote.

items.question: Why can two cars get different prices for the same tint?
items.answer: Because the same tint is rarely the same job. One car might have clean glass, the other four windows of old film that has bubbled or gone purple. Removing old film is real work done before the new film goes on, and it is a common reason two similar cars land at different numbers.

items.question: Do I need an appointment, or do you take walk-ins?
items.answer: We recommend calling ahead so we can have your film and a bay ready, but walk-ins are welcome if there is room.

items.question: Is there a warranty?
items.answer: Yes. Lifetime manufacturer warranty on the window film.

items.question: What if something goes wrong with my film later?
items.answer: Call or text us and bring the vehicle back, or tell us about the room. The film carries a lifetime manufacturer warranty on the film, and we have been at the same shop in Boulder City since 1994, so we are not hard to find later.

items.question: What areas do you serve?
items.answer: Boulder City, Henderson, Las Vegas, and Southern Nevada. Vehicles come to our Boulder City shop; for homes and offices we come to you.

items.question: Do you come to my home or business?
items.answer: Yes, for home and office film and blinds: we come to you to measure and install. Vehicles need to come to our Boulder City shop.

items.question: How long has BC Glass & Tint been in business?
items.answer: We are a family-owned shop that has served Boulder City and Southern Nevada since 1994.

items.question: Is window tint legal in Nevada?
items.answer: Yes, within limits. Film on your front side windows has to let through not less than 35 percent of light, with a 7 percent tolerance, counting the glass and the film together, and it has to be nonreflective. The windshield can only carry a strip across the very top, and that strip cannot be red or amber. Your back side windows and rear window can be tinted as long as the vehicle has outside mirrors on both sides. Source: Nevada Revised Statutes 484D.440.

items.question: What is the difference between ceramic and carbon film?
items.answer: Ceramic film handles more of the sun's infrared without going darker, and it does not interfere with phone, GPS or radio signals the way older metallic films did. Every film we install is ceramic.

items.question: Will tint help keep my car cooler?
items.answer: Yes, it helps. Ceramic film turns away part of the sun's infrared heat at the glass, so the cabin stays more comfortable and your air conditioning does not have to work as hard.

items.question: How long does an install take?
items.answer: Most vehicles are done the same day.

items.question: How long until I can roll my windows down?
items.answer: Give the film a few days to fully cure before lowering your windows. In summer heat about 24 hours is usually enough, and on cooler days give it longer.

items.question: How do I care for my tint after it is installed?
items.answer: For the first few days do not roll the windows down. After that, wait about a week before cleaning the film, then use a soft cloth and a mild, ammonia-free cleaner. Ammonia-based products can haze or lift the film over time.

items.question: Does my car glass already block UV, or do I still need tint?
items.answer: Your windshield already does much of the work. Laminated windshield glass blocks over 90 percent of UVA. Your side windows are a different kind of glass and can let up to half of it through. That gap is what window film closes. Source: The Skin Cancer Foundation.

items.question: What does a tint percentage like 35 percent mean?
items.answer: It is how much visible light comes through. VLT, or visible light transmission, is the percentage of light that passes through the glass and the film together. A higher number is lighter, a lower number is darker. It measures light only, not heat.

items.question: Is darker tint always better at blocking heat?
items.answer: No. How dark a film looks is about visible light. How much heat it turns away depends on how it handles infrared, which your eye cannot see. A lighter film can perform in the same range as a much darker one, which matters here because Nevada limits how dark your front side windows may be.

items.question: Does window film go on the inside or the outside of the glass?
items.answer: The inside, on vehicles and on buildings alike. Keeping it inside protects it from rain, road grit and washing.

items.question: Why does my new tint look hazy or have small water pockets?
items.answer: That is curing, and it is normal. Some of the water used to position the film has to work its way out afterward. As it evaporates the haze clears and small pockets settle. Give it a few days.

items.question: Will film make my house or office too dark?
items.answer: No. Light, nearly clear films are available that keep your view and natural light while cutting glare and UV.

items.question: Does sunlight through my windows really fade furniture and flooring?
items.answer: Yes. The same rays that fade furnishings, flooring and fabric keep working on a mild day, not only a hot one. Cutting that exposure is one of the main reasons people put film on a west-facing room. Source: The Skin Cancer Foundation.

items.question: Can it help lower cooling bills?
items.answer: It can help. Film turns away part of the sun's heat at the glass, so a sunny room stays more comfortable and your air conditioning does not have to fight the sun as hard. We do not promise a number on your bill, because what you see depends on your home and your glass.

items.question: Can you do large storefronts and offices?
items.answer: Yes. We give free quotes for offices, retail, restaurants and more, including security and privacy film.

items.question: How does the process work?
items.answer: You call, text or request a time. We measure and give you a free quote, walk you through the film options, and book your install date. For blinds and shades we measure at your windows and order to those measurements. On the day, the work is usually done in a single visit.

items.question: Should I repair or replace a chip or crack?
items.answer: If it is a small chip or a small crack, we check it first and can usually fill and seal it before it spreads. When the damage is too large to repair, the replacement is arranged with a glass specialist we work with, with the glass ordered to your VIN.

items.question: Will insurance cover a full windshield replacement?
items.answer: It can, and it depends on your policy rather than on us. Comprehensive coverage is what usually applies. We can help you work through the claim; bring your policy details when you call.

items.question: How fast is a windshield replacement?
items.answer: Same day means the same day as your scheduled appointment, not the day you call. Chip repair we do in our own shop; a full replacement is arranged with a glass specialist we work with. We do not keep windshields in stock, so the glass is ordered to your VIN and the appointment is booked for after it arrives, usually within the week.

items.question: Is clear bra really invisible?
items.answer: Nearly. It is a clear urethane paint protection film with a self-healing top coat. It takes rock chips and road debris, and light scratches fade with heat from the sun. Partial or full coverage is available.

items.question: How long will my car be at the shop for a ceramic coating?
items.answer: Usually two to four days, depending on the car. The paint is decontaminated and corrected before anything is bonded to it, and we keep the vehicle a further 24 hours while the coating cures.

items.question: What do I need to avoid after a ceramic coating?
items.answer: Keep it dry while it finishes curing. For the first 24 hours to three days, depending on conditions, do not wash the vehicle, do not park it where sprinklers can reach it, and try to keep it out of the rain. We will tell you the exact window for your car when you pick it up.

items.question: What kinds of blinds do you install?
items.answer:
Three main styles, plus motorized options on any of them, all measured at your windows and ordered to those measurements.
  • Cellular shades. The cells hold a pocket of air between you and the glass, which slows the heat coming through. The best insulator of the three.
  • Roller shades. A single flat panel in a range of openness: a tighter weave blocks more glare, a more open weave keeps your view.
  • Roman shades. Fabric that gathers into soft folds as it lifts; the decorative choice.
  • Motorized, on any of the above. No cords, and tall or hard to reach windows go on a remote or a schedule.

items.question: Are custom blinds done the same day like the tint work?
items.answer: No. Blinds and shades are measured at your windows and then ordered to those measurements, so there is a wait between the measure and the install. We will tell you the expected timing when we measure.

items.question: Can cloudy or yellowed headlights be fixed, or do I need new ones?
items.answer: In most cases they can be restored, for a fraction of the cost of new housings. Headlight lenses are plastic, and the Nevada sun breaks down the factory coating until the lens goes cloudy and yellow. Restoration removes the damaged surface layer, then a protective clear layer goes over the fresh surface. For longer protection we can apply clear film over the lenses instead.

items.question: How much does headlight restoration cost?
items.answer: It comes down to how oxidized the lenses are, how many lights need work, and whether film goes on afterward. Call or text us the vehicle and, if you can, a photo of the headlights, for a free quote.

items.question: How long does headlight restoration take?
items.answer: Most vehicles are done the same day. If you want protection film over the lenses afterward, that is best done at the same visit.

items.question: Can you tint or smoke my headlights and taillights?
items.answer: Yes, in legal-depth smoke. How dark depends on your housings and how much light they put out, so we look at your vehicle rather than quoting a percentage. Nevada requires a tail lamp to emit a red light plainly visible from 500 feet to the rear.
